value.rationale: For a canonical high-degree two-community social network, the complete basins quantify whether local self-retaining majority yields stable coexistence, consensus or nonconvergent two-phase polarization. The nonzero one-half asymptotic swapping probability despite diverging degrees, parity-amplified frozen-state rare event, and explicit N^{-1/2} initial-bias crossover give motivated statistical information not provided by generic period-two bounds or the source mean-field treatment. The exact classification is natural rather than an arbitrary small parameter slice.
